messages:
Chloe Martin: Hey folks — sharing the updated postmortem template section for the incident taxonomy rollout. Would love eyes on:
1) are the taxonomy fields short enough?
2) is ownership assignment explicit enough?

Draft (Confluence sandbox): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/pm-template-taxonomy-v1

Changes are basically:
- Add “Incident metadata (taxonomy)” block
- Require `Category`, `Impacted surface`, `Primary owner (team)`
- Add `Contributing factors` + `Customer tier` as optional
- Add “Remediation SLA” block (TTM/TTR targets + actuals)

Please comment inline or here.

Miles Thornton: :eyes: skimming now. First reaction: the taxonomy block is good but we should keep it to 3 required fields max. During writeup folks will already be tired.

Maybe:
Required:
- Category (single select)
- Primary owning team (single select)
- Impacted surface (single select)

Optional:
- Contributing factors (multi)
- Region(s)
- Customer tier

If we add 6+ required fields, people will skip/half-fill.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also: make “Primary owner (team)” not just free text. We keep getting “Platform” / “Infra?” / “SRE???” in postmortems and it’s impossible to trend.

Can we align with the incident-bot values so it’s literally the same dropdown list?

Allison Grant: From observability side, yes please. If the postmortem template uses different strings than the incident intake, our dashboards will be garbage.

If template can say:
- Category: (must match taxonomy v1 allowed values)
- Owning team: (must match ownership map allowed values)
- Impacted surface: (must match incident metadata standard)

Then postmortem data is joinable.

Sean Gallagher: Also want to avoid the “owner = IC” anti-pattern. Owner should be the team that will actually fix the root cause, not whoever wrote the doc.

Maybe add a line right under the field:
> Primary owner is the team responsible for the primary fix (not the incident commander).

Chloe Martin: Got it. The current draft has “Owner” but not “team”. I can change label to “Primary owner (team)” and add that hint text.

Aisha Bello: Re: SLA block — love it, but can we make it frictionless?

Suggestion: template auto-populates targets based on Sev + Category + Tier, and the author only fills in actuals.

If we can’t auto-populate yet, at least make “Target TTM / Target TTR” a copy-paste table from the mapping doc.

Devon Price: We can’t auto-populate in Confluence template today (unless we build a macro or do some hack). But we *can*:
- link the SLA mapping table
- include a short lookup hint (“See Remediation SLA mapping; use row matching Sev/Category/Tier”)

Also, for taxonomy values, we can include the canonical list in the template as a small collapsed section.

Dev Patel: Support perspective: please keep “Customer impact summary” section separate from taxonomy. People keep burying the key info in metadata fields.

Also for ownership: can we include escalation contact? Like “Owning team Slack channel” or “On-call rotation”? Helps Support when we’re reading older PMs.

Miles Thornton: I’d keep escalation out of the postmortem template. That’s more runbook / ownership map territory. Otherwise template balloons.

But we can include one link:
> Ownership map + escalation: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/ownership-map

Jasmine Liu: Agree with Miles. If you add escalation fields, people will fill them wrong and it’ll rot. Link to source of truth.

But strongly +1 to making owner explicit because customer comms always asks “who’s on point for follow-ups” and we waste time figuring it out.

Priya Natarajan: Another minor thing: make sure “Impacted surface” includes dedicated/private distinctions.

We keep having PMs written as if “API down” means hosted only, but it was actually 2 dedicated pools in us-east.

So surface values should include:
- Hosted API
- Dedicated pools
- Private (Redwood-operated)
- Console
- Control plane
…etc (whatever the metadata standard says).

Allison Grant: +1. The incident metadata standard already has “Deployment mode” vs “Surface” as separate concepts. We decided to keep the required fields minimal in v1, so surface should be the user-visible thing, and “Deployment mode” can be optional.

Chloe Martin: OK. So I’ll:
- Keep required fields to 3: Category / Impacted surface / Primary owner (team)
- Ensure labels match incident metadata standard and incident-bot allowed values
- Add hint text “owner team != IC”
- Link to ownership map + SLA mapping
- Make “Deployment mode / Region / Customer tier / Contributing factors” optional

Anything else?

Rafael Mendes: One more ask: put the taxonomy block near the top (right after Summary) so it’s not missed. People stop halfway through.

Sean Gallagher: And maybe add a checkbox in the “Action items” section: “Action items include owner team + due date + SLA (TTM/TTR) if applicable.” We keep shipping vague action items.

Miles Thornton: For action items, can we just enforce “owner + due date” and not tie to SLA? SLA is incident-level; action items are tasks.

Aisha Bello: Agree — keep action items simple. But for SLA tracking, we should at least include:
- Mitigation completed at:
- Permanent fix completed at:
- If missed target, why (capacity/complexity/coordination)

That’s useful in monthly review.

Devon Price: Also we should standardize the “Category changed after incident” note. We saw it in the trial incident — the bot said “capacity exhaustion” but PM said “routing overload”.

Maybe add a small field:
- Category at declare time:
- Final category:

But that might be too much.

Allison Grant: I’d keep only “Final category” required. If you want to capture drift, we can compare against incident record in the system once pipeline is in place. Don’t ask humans twice.

Chloe Martin: Makes sense. I’ll keep just “Final category” and we’ll rely on the ingestion pipeline later for declare-time value.

Dev Patel: Works for me.

Chloe Martin: Cool — I’ll update the draft today and post again for final pass. Targeting rollout next week in #postmortems (with a reminder that old PMs don’t need retro edits unless we’re doing the 90-day backfill).

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: thanks Chloe

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: (and please ping me if you want the exact allowed value strings)

Chloe Martin: Will do — grabbing from the metadata standard page + incident-bot config.

(edited) Chloe Martin: Updated draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/pm-template-taxonomy-v1
Changes made per feedback:
- Required: Category / Impacted surface / Primary owner (team)
- Owner hint text + link to ownership map
- SLA block simplified (targets link + actuals fields)
- Optional fields moved into collapsed section

If no objections by EOD tomorrow I’ll mark as final.

Rafael Mendes: Looks good now. The required block is tight.

Priya Natarajan: Approved from me.

Jasmine Liu: +1 good. The “owner team != IC” line is exactly what we need.

Devon Price: Approved. I’ll make sure incident-bot uses the same strings so we don’t drift.

Chloe Martin: Great — closing loop. I’ll announce rollout once it’s published.

System message: Chloe Martin marked this thread as resolved.
